subject: Civil Engineering
title: Change Orders
description: Learn Change Orders in one minute.

hook.text: The owner wants an extra floor. The soil is worse than expected. Plans must change.

buildup.text: A change order modifies the original contract — adding scope, time, or cost.

discovery.text: Each change order must be priced, negotiated, and approved before the work proceeds.

twist.text: Contractors sometimes bid low, expecting to profit from change orders — a common industry tactic.

climax.text: Boston's Big Dig had over 7,000 change orders — costs ballooned from $2.8B to $14.6B.

punchline.text: Every change costs more than the original plan. The cheapest change is the one you avoid.

quiz.question: Why did Boston's Big Dig cost five times its original estimate?
options: Inflation raised material costs dramatically during construction
Over 7,000 change orders accumulated, each adding scope, time, and cost
The project was redesigned from scratch three times
